outputs.explanation: Scatter plot where each of the 141 points is an individual sample measurement; individual data points are the data itself.
Each marker represents the mean ± s.d. of 6 replicate samples per reporter; the underlying individual replicate values are not shown, only the averaged point with error bars.
Panel shows fitted distribution/density curves (line-plot type) of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes; line plots are exempt from requiring overlaid individual points.
Box plots are exempt from this check by definition, and individual sample data points are additionally overlaid on the boxes.

Polar histograms display the distribution of raw phase-difference measurements per cell line (with n indicated), functioning as histograms rather than averaged bar/mean plots, so overlay of individual points is not required.

This polar histogram shows subtype-level averages computed across 1-4 underlying cell-line distributions (shown individually in panel E) without overlaying or otherwise indicating those individual cell-line values.
This is a single illustrative example of raw signal data with a fitted curve, not an averaged summary plot, so individual data point overlay is not applicable.
Scatter plot where each of the 117 samples is plotted individually (error bars reflect fit parameter uncertainty, not inter-sample averaging), so individual data points are shown.
